arguments.root_cause_explanation: The incident was caused by a network configuration rollout that altered BGP reachability for a concentrated set of locations. Inspected metrics (EV003‑EV007) show all affected services had only 14 of 21 BGP sessions up and an HTTP success rate of ~2 %, indicating traffic was being blocked at the edge. The configuration snapshot (EV023) captured the new route policy at the time of the outage. The scan (EV002) reported svc-015 unavailable while other independent paths remained reachable, matching the pattern of a targeted reachability change. Rolling back that configuration (repair R02) restored 11 of the 12 initially failed services with zero new outages, confirming the hypothesis.
arguments.rationale: The root cause H02 (network configuration rollout) best explains the observed BGP session reduction and selective service unavailability. Repair R02 (roll‑back and redeploy stable config) is the lowest‑cost (cost 4, risk low) action that fully restores the initially unavailable services without introducing new failures, as demonstrated by the simulation and apply_repair results.
